title: Extreme ownership
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Why don't you have what you say you want, and where is the answer: inside or outside?

Jose said: if I say to you: why don't you have a hundred million dollars in your bank account, assuming you want it? A student answered: I found ten thousand ways not to make a light bulb, and I'm coming up on the one way to make it.
Jose said: you made a connection between your progress internally and how you are affecting your external. Is it something I am creating internally in my personality that is creating my circumstance?

He would say, Jose said: I don't have a hundred million dollars because I'm not in control of my external circumstances, so I must have something internally wrong that I haven't achieved. A student said: he is taking extreme ownership and responsibility for everything.

Nothing externally is at fault for my circumstances, Jose said. That is one way to look at things. I don't have the money I should have in my bank account because I am doing something wrong. That is extreme ownership.

A student said that if a culture gives people excuses, it is reinforcing a lack of responsibility in individual decision-making. In an effort to empower people it is actually disempowering them, by making everything else's fault.

Jose said: they have given them a thousand excuses, the psychology and the empathy and the mental health, a thousand excuses for how they can't control their environment. A student said: how they can't work hard, and can't accomplish anything.
What would you say to yourself if the answer was only inside?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one thing you want that you don't have.
Write what you would change inside to get it.
Write the excuses you give most.
Write what ownership of it would look like.
Write one external fact that is true and still not an excuse.

check.q: What did a student call the approach of blaming nothing external?
What did a student say about a culture that gives people excuses?
choices: It disempowers them by making everything else's fault

check.q: What did a student say about finding ten thousand ways?
choices: They are coming up on the one way that works

recap: Look at what you do inside before you blame what is outside. Own the result.
